paper_metadata.title: Identifying Relations for Open Information Extraction
paper_metadata.venue: Proceedings of the 2011 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP 2011)
paper_metadata.abstract: The paper identifies incoherent and uninformative extractions in Open Information Extraction systems and introduces syntactic and lexical constraints on binary verbal relation phrases. The constraints are implemented in ReVerb, which substantially improves precision-recall performance over earlier Open IE extractors.

problem_addressed: The paper addresses incoherent relation phrases and uninformative extractions produced by open-domain relation extractors such as TextRunner and WOE. Its objective is to design simple, scalable constraints that produce more coherent and informative binary verbal relations while retaining broad Web-scale coverage.

methodology.description: ReVerb operates on POS-tagged and noun-phrase-chunked sentences. For each verb, it identifies the longest contiguous relation phrase matching a verb-centered POS regular expression and passing a lexical frequency constraint. It merges adjacent or overlapping matches, then selects the nearest valid noun phrase to the left and right as arguments. A logistic regression classifier assigns extraction confidence. The lexical dictionary is built offline from 500 million Web sentences; relation phrases are normalized and retained when they take at least 20 distinct argument pairs, yielding approximately 1.7 million normalized phrases.

ontology_or_schema_use.value: No fixed ontology or relation vocabulary is required. ReVerb uses a corpus-derived dictionary of relation phrases and syntactic/lexical constraints over binary verbal relations; the resulting relations remain open-domain surface phrases.

input_output.input_type: Unstructured English Web sentences; the relation dictionary is induced from a corpus of 500 million Web sentences, and evaluation uses Web sentences with additional training examples from Wikipedia.
input_output.input_granularity: Sentence-level; extraction is performed on individual POS-tagged, NP-chunked sentences.
input_output.output_representation: Binary extraction triples (x, r, y), where x and y are noun-phrase arguments and r is a contiguous verbal relation phrase; each extraction also receives a confidence score.

Verb-centered POS regular expression for syntactic filtering
Corpus-derived lexical relation dictionary with phrase normalization
Compared systems: TextRunner, TextRunner-R, WOEpos, WOEparse
datasets: 500 million Web sentences for constructing the lexical dictionary
500 Web sentences sampled with Yahoo’s random link service for intrinsic evaluation
1,000 Web and Wikipedia sentences manually labeled for confidence training
Penn Treebank sentences for generating TextRunner-R training examples
67,562 positive and 356,834 negative TextRunner-R training instances
Banko and Etzioni’s 500 million Web-sentence corpus for scale evaluation

evaluation.setting: Intrinsic comparison on 500 randomly sampled Web sentences. Two human judges labeled each extraction correct or incorrect; only cases where they concurred were used for reported precision-recall results. Confidence thresholds generated precision-recall curves and AUC values. Additional experiments measured speed on 100,000 sentences and precision at frequency thresholds on a 500-million-sentence corpus.

value: ReVerb achieved an AUC 30% higher than WOEparse and more than twice the AUC of WOEpos and TextRunner.
ReVerb’s AUC was 23% higher than ReVerb¬lex; removing the lexical constraint reduced performance.
TextRunner-R achieved an AUC 71% higher than TextRunner and performed on par with WOEpos, but remained below ReVerb.
More than 30% of ReVerb extractions were at precision 0.8 or higher, compared with virtually none for the other systems.
WOEparse had slightly higher recall than ReVerb (0.64 versus 0.62) but lower precision.
In the relation-phrase-only evaluation, ReVerb had higher precision and recall than the compared systems.
On 100,000 sentences, ReVerb took 16 minutes, TextRunner and WOEpos each took 21 minutes, and WOEparse took 11 hours.
At scale, ReVerb achieved precision 0.75 for frequency-1 extractions; TextRunner could not approach this even at frequency 10, where its precision was 0.34.

value: Simple syntactic and lexical constraints substantially reduce incoherent and uninformative extractions.
Relation phrases are identified holistically rather than by independent word-level decisions.
The corpus-derived lexical constraint supports open-domain extraction without a fixed relation inventory.
The shallow implementation is substantially faster than the dependency-parser baseline in the reported speed test.
The method retains useful recall while greatly improving precision over earlier Open IE systems.
Review-level inference: binary triples provide a straightforward intermediate representation for downstream knowledge-graph construction.

value: Argument-finding heuristics account for 65% of incorrect ReVerb extractions.

The constraints miss some valid relations: 15% of manually identified binary verbal relation phrases failed the constraints.
The method misses relations because of incorrect argument identification, lexical filtering, overly specific alternative relations, and POS/chunking errors.

value: The constraints are an idealized model of English relation phrases and do not cover all valid relations.
The method misses non-contiguous phrases, phrases not between their arguments, and phrases that do not match the POS pattern.
Deeper syntactic analysis could model long-range dependencies more flexibly but would increase processing time and, according to the authors’ observations, can reduce precision on Web text.
ReVerb models binary relations and therefore mishandles n-ary relations expressed by ditransitive verbs.
Incorrect argument extraction is the dominant source of both incorrect and missed extractions.
The authors identify improved argument extraction and combining the constraints with constrained CRF learning as future directions.
